text: Almost midnight... and this is the only way home.
note: Its own file (assets/voice.mp3), not in the sound pack.

text: Someone's been burning offerings. [beat] Is it Seventh Month already?
There's one right at my feet. Like it was left for me.
[a sharp, frightened inhale] Oh my God.
note: Meant as a wordless gasp; the take also says the words (found by transcription at v5.14, as vrelief's were at v4.8).

text: [a short, dismissive laugh] It's just paper.
note: Meant as a wordless scoff; the take also says the words (found by transcription at v5.14).

text: [running out of breath] No, no, no, no, no.
note: Meant as wordless panting; the take also says the words (found by transcription at v5.14).

text: [a quiet, shaken exhale — no words]
note: Wordless since v4.8 (the first take turned out to say 'Just keep walking. Don't look back').

text: Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa. I'm sorry. I'll go.
note: Retired at v3.7's cutscene pass; the file is still in the shared pack. Transcribed from the shipped take at v5.14.

text: It's just paper. [beat] So why does my hand feel like it's holding something heavier?
[panting] I shouldn't have done that. I knew it the second my foot touched it.
Look first. That's all it takes. Just... look first.
Not my offering. Not my business. [exhale] Rest well, whoever you are.
Am I... seeing things?
Ahh!
No no no
Who's there?!
What is that
[shaky breathing] My chest... I need to get out of here. Now.
No... my head... everything's... spinning...
[terrified whisper] I can't... I can't be here... [panicked breathing] No. No. No.
It followed me home.
Ma? Ma, is that you?
There is someone in the room.
It keeps coming from over there, from the wall.
I have slept beside that gap my whole life. Never has this happened.
MA! MA, COME HERE! PLEASE!
It was already looking at me. It had been the whole time.
She did not even ask what was wrong. She just left.
I'm leaving this room. I will sleep in the living room tonight.
Nothing happened. That is not the same as nothing being there.
They put the tent up on Monday. It is still going.
My mother told me not to come down. I came down anyway.
Everyone seems fascinated by the performance...
note: Re-said in Chad's words at v4.5.

text: That one is looking at me. Nobody else is.
note: Lost its place when the ghost left the chapter (v4.3); the file is still in chapter 3's pack.

text: There's one chair facing the wrong way. Just one.
She's out there! Standing outside...
note: Re-said in Chad's words at v4.5.

text: She's not coming in.
I feel better here... but why?
note: Re-said in Chad's words at v4.5.

text: He has not blinked. Not once.
He looked at me. Out of all of them... he looked at me.
His eyes were shut. He was looking at me with his eyes shut.
Is it real, auntie?
I could still hear the drum from the lift. I told myself that was normal.
I did not move. He looked at me anyway.
I knew better. I went up there anyway.
She told me the truth. Both halves of it.
I got out. The drum stopped when I did.
I stayed outside the whole day. Anywhere but here.
Ma's working late. The flat is empty.
One quiet night. That's all I want.
I can do this.
Sit down. Breathe. Think it through.
Start from the beginning.
The void deck. The hell note. Where it started.
Then my own room. The gap beside my bed. It wasn't random.
Same block. Same week. Same me. It's not the places — it's following me.
Enough. I'm tired. It's nothing — every block has its stories.
...the clock. Why can't I hear the clock?
You want me?! I'm right here! Come out where I can SEE you!
okay... okay. stupid. stupid. stupid me...
Ma. It's me... no— something's wrong with the flat.
I know how it sounds. Please.
It was never random. It followed me home.
I ignored it. It did not ignore me.
I dared it. In my own home. It answered.
Help is coming tomorrow. I can hold one night.
He actually came.
Why is he bowing at the kitchen.
That's the hell note. From the void deck. It's been here the whole time.
Do I...approach him?
He walked around the flat like he's reading it.
Uncle. What did you see?
I should never have asked for help. I sound...crazy.
note: Shaky. Transcribed from the shipped take at v5.14.

text: Paper. It's just paper.
The first one. He says every case teaches you the next.
I asked him what to learn. He told me. All of it.
The fear followed me into the morning. When will it go away?
I called it paper. She heard me.
It's over. [beat] It's really over.
